sources.quote: Google's own guidance lists review count and quality among the prominence signals for the map pack
sources.title: Tips to improve your local ranking on Google - Google Business Profile Help
sources.evidence: Local results are mainly based on relevance, distance, and popularity. Prominence means how well-known a business is. This factor is based on info like how many websites link to your business and how many reviews you have. More reviews and positive ratings can help your business's local ranking.

sources.quote: prohibit review gating (only asking customers you know are happy), incentives of any kind, reviews from employees or family
sources.publisher: Google Maps User Generated Content Policy Help
sources.title: Prohibited & restricted content - Maps User Generated Content Policy Help
sources.evidence: Google prohibits offering incentives, such as payment, discounts, free goods and/or services, in exchange for posting any review or revision or removal of a negative review. Merchants are prohibited from discouraging or prohibiting negative reviews, or selectively soliciting positive reviews from customers. A conflict of interest may include current or former employment, a contractual or consultory relationship, or other professional or personal affiliations (such as industry competitors, familial relationships, etc.).

sources.quote: Violations can get reviews removed or your profile suspended.
sources.title: Business Profile restrictions for policy violations - Google Business Profile Help
sources.evidence: If a business owner has violated Google's Fake Engagement policy, Google might place restrictions on their Business Profile, including preventing the profile from receiving new reviews or ratings for a set period of time. Flagged reviews that violate content policies are removed and will no longer show on Maps and Search.

sources.quote: treats fake or misleading reviews and undisclosed incentives as deceptive marketing
sources.title: The Deceptive Marketing Practices Digest — Volume 1
sources.evidence: Astroturfing, when used in an advertising context, refers to the practice of creating commercial representations that masquerade as the authentic experiences and opinions of impartial consumers, such as fake consumer reviews and testimonials. Under the Competition Act, it is against the law to advertise or market something in a way that is false or misleading.

sources.quote: penalties can reach into the millions for corporations
sources.title: Penalties and remedies for non-compliance
sources.evidence: On first occurrence, individuals are liable to penalties of up to $750,000 and corporations are liable to penalties of up to $10,000,000; for corporations the penalty is up to the greater of $10 million ($15 million for each subsequent violation) and three times the value of the benefit derived from the deceptive conduct, or 3% of the corporation's annual worldwide gross revenues.

sources.quote: Flag reviews that violate Google's policies (competitor sabotage, reviews from people who were never customers, hate speech, off-topic rants) through your profile
sources.title: Report inappropriate reviews on your Business Profile - Google Business Profile Help
sources.evidence: To report a review on your Business Profile, go to your Business Profile, select Read reviews, next to the review you'd like to flag select Report, select the reason to flag the review, and then select Send report. You can report any review, but only those that violate Google policies are eligible for removal. If a flagged review doesn't qualify for removal, you can submit a one-time appeal.

flags.quote: Add Review or AggregateRating schema so Google can show star ratings in search results
flags.issue: Google's review snippet documentation states that self-serving reviews are no longer displayed for businesses and organizations: if the entity being reviewed controls the reviews about itself (reviews placed on its own site, directly in structured data or through an embedded Google or Facebook reviews widget), pages using LocalBusiness or Organization structured data are ineligible for the star review feature. Adding Review or AggregateRating markup to a business's own homepage and service pages will not produce star ratings in search results.
